cr-1.1-re1.reasoning: Every operator and technician logs in with a personal account; there is no shared login.

cr-1.10.reasoning: PIN and password entry on the touch panel is masked.

cr-1.11.reasoning: After five failed logins the account is locked for 15 minutes; the limit is configurable.

cr-1.12.reasoning: The HMI shows a configurable notice before the login screen.

cr-1.7.reasoning: Minimum length, complexity and lifetime of passwords are configurable; the defaults follow NIST SP 800-63B.

cr-2.10.reasoning: On an audit write error the controller keeps running and raises a maintenance alarm to SCADA.

cr-2.11.reasoning: Audit records carry a UTC time stamp from the real-time clock.

cr-2.11-re1.reasoning: The real-time clock is synchronised with the plant NTP server every hour.

cr-2.4.reasoning: Neither the PLC nor the HMI runtime loads scripts, plug-ins or other mobile code.

cr-2.8-re1.reasoning: Only the administrator role can disable audit categories; the change itself is logged.

cr-2.9.reasoning: 4 MB of flash are reserved for the audit log as a ring buffer; a full log never stops pump control.

cr-3.13.reasoning: Trust anchors are provisioned by the vendor at production; owner provisioning is planned for firmware 2.0.

cr-3.8.reasoning: HMI session IDs are 128-bit random values and are invalidated at logout and on timeout.

cr-6.1.reasoning: The audit log can be read, read-only, over OPC UA by the maintenance role and exported as CSV.

cr-7.3-re1.reasoning: Configuration backups carry a signature that is checked before a restore.

cr-7.6.reasoning: A secure-defaults profile can be applied from the HMI; the current settings can be viewed there.

info.description: Industrial pump station controller (PLC with HMI, configuration store, service and fieldbus interfaces) evaluated against the CRA edition of IEC 62443-4-2 (EN IEC 62443-4-2/prAA, draft). Shows the requirement matrix with met, planned, stated, open and gap rows.
info.name: Pump Station Controller

assumptions.text: The cabinet is locked; only the maintenance team holds the key.
The plant IT network is untrusted; the utility maintains the firewall between it and the control network.
Vendor remote access is only possible through the utility's gateway, approved per ticket.

functions.description: Keeps pressures and levels by driving pumps and valves.
functions.name: Pump control

functions.description: Reports process values and alarms to the HMI and SCADA.
functions.name: Monitoring

functions.description: Program download, firmware update, remote and local service.
functions.name: Service and update

functions.description: Initial firmware via JTAG, then fused off; secrets into the secure element.
functions.name: Production programming

functions.description: Overwrites recipes, configuration and credentials before disposal.
functions.name: Factory reset

architecture.text: The PLC runs the pump control on an RTOS with an OPC UA server towards HMI, SCADA and engineering and a Modbus RTU master towards the field; recipes and configuration are kept in signed flash records. See the DFD.

boundary.text: The controller in its cabinet: HMI runtime, pump controller (PLC), configuration store and the cabinet's interfaces (touch panel, service USB, Ethernet, fieldbus, JTAG). Not part of it: SCADA, the vendor's update server and gateway, the engineering workstation and the pumps and valves in the field.

constraints.text: Cyber Resilience Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/2847) with EN IEC 62443-4-2 (draft prAA) as the harmonised standard, SL-T 2 for the station's zone; drinking-water regulations of the operator.

environment.text: Pump station of a water utility: locked building, controller in a locked cabinet, control network of the station behind the utility's firewall; vendor service only through the utility's remote access gateway.

risks.attackDescription: Attacker injects malformed or malicious input data that causes the process to behave incorrectly
risks.causeDescription: Insufficient input validation — the process accepts data without verifying its integrity

proposedMitigations.text: Implement integrity controls and checksums
Use digital signatures for data integrity
Implement input validation and data sanitization

proposedVerifications.text: Integrity check validation testing
Code review for buffer overflow vulnerabilities

risks.threatDescription: Process input tampering — attacker modifies input data to alter process behavior

risks.attackDescription: Attacker sends high volume of requests consuming all available CPU, memory, or file handles
risks.causeDescription: No resource limits or rate limiting — process allocates unbounded resources in response to requests

proposedMitigations.text: Implement rate limiting and throttling
Implement quotas and resource limits
Use load balancing to distribute traffic

proposedVerifications.text: Stress testing and load testing (k6, JMeter)
DDoS simulation testing
Rate limiting effectiveness testing

risks.threatDescription: Process resource exhaustion — attacker exhausts process resources causing denial of service

risks.attackDescription: Attacker exploits a process vulnerability to execute code or trigger operations with elevated privileges
risks.causeDescription: Insufficient input validation or privilege boundary enforcement in the process

proposedMitigations.text: Apply least privilege principle
Implement proper ACLs and role-based access control
Implement strict input validation
Use sandboxing to isolate processes

proposedVerifications.text: Privilege escalation penetration testing

SAST code review (SonarQube, Checkmarx)

risks.threatDescription: Privilege escalation via process vulnerability — attacker gains elevated privileges through process flaw

risks.attackDescription: Attacker replaces firmware with a malicious version that disables safety interlocks
risks.causeDescription: No cryptographic code signing enforced — unsigned firmware is accepted for execution

proposedMitigations.text: Implement integrity controls and checksums
Implement input validation and data sanitization
Enforce cryptographic code signing — only firmware signed with a trusted key is accepted for execution

proposedVerifications.text: Integrity check validation testing
Code review for buffer overflow vulnerabilities

risks.threatDescription: Embedded firmware tampering — attacker modifies firmware on embedded controller

risks.attackDescription: Attacker floods the OT protocol interface with high-frequency frames starving legitimate traffic
risks.causeDescription: OT protocol stack has no rate limiting — flooding causes processing overload

proposedMitigations.text: Implement rate limiting and throttling
Use ACLs or filtering to restrict access
Use load balancing to distribute traffic
Implement automated backup and tested recovery procedure for system restoration after attack (CR 7.3/7.4)

proposedVerifications.text: Stress testing and load testing (k6, JMeter)
Rate limiting effectiveness testing

risks.threatDescription: OT protocol flooding — attacker floods OT protocol stack causing denial of service

risks.attackDescription: Attacker connects JTAG probe, halts CPU, reads/writes memory and bypasses all software security controls
risks.causeDescription: JTAG interface is accessible and not locked via OTP fuse

proposedMitigations.text: Apply least privilege principle
Disable debug interfaces in production
Physically separate or remove debug interfaces in production units
Implement application whitelisting — only explicitly authorized binaries may execute
Store cryptographic keys and credentials in hardware-protected storage (TPM, Secure Element, HSM)
Implement proper ACLs and role-based access control

proposedVerifications.text: Privilege escalation penetration testing
Physical security inspection of debug interfaces
Verify debug interface is disabled — attempt JTAG/SWD connection and confirm access is denied

risks.threatDescription: JTAG privilege escalation — attacker gains full processor control via JTAG interface

risks.attackDescription: Attacker uses debug interface to modify firmware, configuration, or calibration data
risks.causeDescription: Flash/EEPROM/NVRAM storage lacks access control or integrity protection

proposedMitigations.text: Apply firmware readback protection (RDP Level 1/2 or equivalent OTP mechanism)
Implement integrity controls and checksums
Implement proper ACLs (Access Control Lists)
Enforce hardware access control on storage (MPU memory protection or encryption-as-access-control)

proposedVerifications.text: Verify firmware readback protection level (RDP1/RDP2 or equivalent) is set
Integrity check validation testing

proposedMitigations.text: Apply side-channel countermeasures (power analysis protection, timing attack resistance)

Implement proper ACLs and role-based access control

proposedVerifications.text: Verify side-channel countermeasures are implemented (power analysis, timing)
